entries.title: Morning Briefing · 28 November 2026
headlines: Taiwan votes in nationwide local elections today, with Taipei the main test for President Lai's DPP
New Zealand take control in Christchurch: India 116/6, trailing by 240 after NZ made 356
INDIA bloc meets today to plan its fight over the delimitation bills before Monday's special sitting
DWP takes some online services offline after a cyber incident; payments unaffected
Hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, Reuters reports

stories.headline: Taiwan holds nine-in-one local elections
stories.summary: Taiwan votes today for about 11,000 posts across 22 cities and counties; polls close at 08:00 GMT and results are expected from late morning UK time. The main race is Taipei, where KMT mayor Chiang Wan-an faces the DPP's Puma Shen.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a big test for President Lai Ching-te and the DPP, though local results are a weak guide to the 2028 presidential vote. China flew 33 military sorties around the island on Friday and Saturday.

stories.headline: Hackers breach the US Air Force's Cloud One platform
stories.summary: Reuters reported on Friday that attackers got into Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, which holds personnel and military data. It is the latest in a string of intrusions into US federal systems.
stories.whyItMatters: Who was behind it and what data was taken have not been confirmed publicly.

stories.headline: Israeli strike targets the family of Hamas leader al-Hayya in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on Friday hit the family of Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya; his son Izzeldeen survived, though several relatives were wounded, according to Hamas sources. Israeli attacks killed four other Palestinians elsewhere in Gaza the same day.
stories.whyItMatters: Such strikes strain the October 2025 ceasefire. Gaza's Health Ministry says at least 1,705 people have been killed since the truce began.

stories.headline: Ukraine: Kushner says peace talks are deadlocked over territory
stories.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner said talks have hit a deadlock over Ukrainian land and that Putin has agreed not to use nuclear weapons. Zelensky's warning that Russia is preparing a new mass strike on energy and logistics still stands; no such strike had been reported in the sources checked.
stories.whyItMatters: Kyiv's gains in Kharkiv have not shifted the core dispute over land, and a winter strike on the grid would hit civilians hard.

stories.headline: DWP pulls some online services after a cyber incident
stories.summary: The Department for Work and Pensions took some services offline as a precaution on Friday, including Universal Credit applications, account sign-ins and job search, and is working with the National Cyber Security Centre. There was no evidence on Friday that claimants' personal data had been stolen.
stories.whyItMatters: Pension and benefit payments are not affected and will be paid as normal.

stories.headline: Government brings the EU reset deal to Parliament
stories.summary: The European Partnership Bill, introduced on Thursday, would put the UK-EU reset into law, including an SPS food and farming agreement that removes most post-Brexit checks and a link between the UK and EU carbon trading schemes. A Commons debate is expected on 7 December, and the Conservatives and Reform UK say they would seek repeal.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the biggest legal change to UK-EU trade since Brexit, but it is not law until Parliament passes it.

stories.headline: Grid issues a fourth tight-supply warning in a week
stories.summary: The electricity system operator has issued its fourth tight-supply warning in a week. The Times counts 13 such warnings this year, more than in the previous five years combined.
stories.whyItMatters: Tight margins push up the cost of balancing the grid, which feeds into household bills.

stories.headline: Tory candidates must pledge to leave the ECHR
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch has told prospective Conservative candidates they must sign a pledge backing withdrawal from the European Convention on Human Rights and the repeal of Net Zero laws.
stories.whyItMatters: It sets a clear dividing line with Labour on human rights law, which shapes future debate on asylum and deportation.

stories.headline: Opposition plans its strategy on the delimitation bills
stories.summary: INDIA bloc leaders meet today to agree a joint line on the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill and the Delimitation (Second) Bill before the special sitting opens on Monday 30 November. Congress has issued a three-line whip; the NCP (SP) has backed the revised bill and the DMK has not said how it will vote.
stories.whyItMatters: The revised bill meets the DMK's main demands, so its vote is likely to decide whether the government reaches two-thirds. A similar bill failed in April.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules, fees or visa changes overnight
stories.summary: HC 584 of 3 September is still the latest Statement of Changes. Earned settlement, announced on 2 November with a 10-year default route to ILR, 5 years for people earning over 50,271 pounds and some public service workers, and 3 years for the highest earners, still has no detailed rules, start dates or transitional arrangements laid.
stories.whyItMatters: For Skilled Worker visa holders, including Indian nationals, the current ILR rules still apply.

stories.headline: NZ v India, 2nd Test, day 2: India 116/6, trail by 240
stories.summary: New Zealand resumed on 246/5 and were bowled out for 356, with Akash Deep taking at least four wickets. NZ's seamers then reduced India to 116/6 at stumps, with Dhruv Jurel still in.
stories.whyItMatters: India need 41 more to avoid the follow-on and the series is 0-0. Day 3 starts at 22:00 GMT tonight.

stories.headline: Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 as pressure on Alonso grows
stories.summary: Igor Jesus scored early and Morgan Gibbs-White added a penalty and a second goal for Nottingham Forest; substitute Emmanuel Emegha scored twice for Chelsea.
stories.whyItMatters: Chelsea have lost four of their last five league games under Xabi Alonso, and Forest climb out of the bottom places.

stories.headline: No major space news overnight; Cygnus still set for Sunday
stories.summary: NASA's Cygnus NG-25 cargo launch to the ISS is still targeting 15:47 GMT on Sunday 29 November on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral. ISRO has not announced a date for the uncrewed Gaganyaan G1 flight.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 ends its best week in about eight months
stories.summary: Friday 27 November close: FTSE 100 10,698.81 (+0.84%). Miners led as copper had its best day since February, and banks gained on the Bank of England's lower capital requirements. Markets are closed today.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty fall over 1% as IT stocks are sold
stories.summary: Friday 27 November close: Sensex 83,339.26 (-1.17%), Nifty 50 25,607.20 (-1.07%). The Nifty IT index fell 1.88% while metals rose; profit-taking, US tariff worries and high crude prices weighed.

stories.headline: Wall Street caps its best week since April 2025
stories.summary: Friday 27 November half-day close: S&P 500 7,297.49 (+1.60%), Dow 50,774.94 (+1.18%), Nasdaq Composite 24,129.50 (+2.31%). Over the week the S&P 500 gained 5.6% and the Nasdaq 6.7% as chip and AI stocks rebounded.

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 27 November 2026
headlines: India's Cabinet clears a revised delimitation bill: a uniform 50% rise in Lok Sabha seats, with state shares frozen to 2051, before Monday's special sitting.
Wall Street closes sharply higher in the Black Friday half-day: Nasdaq +2.31%, S&P 500 +1.60%, Dow +1.18%, capping a week of 5-7% gains.
FTSE 100 ends up 0.8% at 10,698.81, its biggest weekly gain in about eight months, as miners and banks rally.
Ukraine says its Kharkiv counteroffensive has retaken about 200 sq km, while Zelensky rejects US land-for-peace options that would cede the Donetsk fortress belt.
Sensex falls 1.17% and Nifty 1.07% as IT stocks are sold off; metals and defence buck the slide.

stories.headline: Ukraine presses its Kharkiv counteroffensive and pushes back on US peace options
stories.summary: Kyiv says Operation Bear Trap in the Kharkiv region has now retaken about 200 sq km and 14 settlements, and is continuing. US negotiators have reportedly put two land-for-peace options to Ukraine; Zelensky rejected giving up the Donetsk fortress belt and said he does not trust a Trump-Putin deal. Jared Kushner said in Berlin that Russia had accepted a weaker form of NATO-style guarantees tied to freezing the front line.
stories.whyItMatters: Battlefield gains strengthen Kyiv's hand just as Washington pushes for a deal. This morning's warning of a new Russian mass strike still stands.

stories.headline: Iran denies the Kuwait drone attack; Saudi-led coalition says it hit 50 Houthi targets
stories.summary: Update on this morning's story: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi denied any role in the drone strike that killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait and offered a joint inquiry with Kuwait and Italy. Saudi Arabia, the UK and the European Commission condemned the attack. The Saudi-led coalition says its strikes in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Saada destroyed 50 military targets, including a launcher used against the Jazan refinery, where a Nepalese worker was killed. Trump said the US has victory at hand against Iran and is giving Tehran a chance to make a deal.
stories.whyItMatters: Attacks on Gulf energy sites keep oil prices high, which feeds through to UK fuel costs and to India's import bill.

stories.headline: Europe: Germany passes a record 2027 budget; Estonia readies Russia border closures
stories.summary: Euronews reports that the Bundestag approved a record 2027 federal budget with about 210 billion euros of borrowing, and that Estonia is preparing to close all five road crossings with Russia. Spain votes in a general election on Sunday, and the conservative leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo says he will step down if he loses.
stories.whyItMatters: Germany is spending heavily on defence and infrastructure while the EU budget talks remain stuck, and the Baltic states keep hardening their borders.

stories.headline: Altria weighs a cash bid for Imperial Brands; shares extend their rally
stories.summary: Imperial Brands rose another 1.8% on Friday after jumping 13.3% on Thursday, when the US tobacco group Altria confirmed it is considering a possible all-cash offer. Under UK takeover rules Altria has until 24 December to make a firm offer or walk away, and Japan Tobacco has also been reported to be studying a deal.
stories.whyItMatters: A bid would be one of the largest takeovers of a FTSE 100 company this year and helped lift the index this week.

stories.headline: Tube strike ends with more trains running than expected
stories.summary: The 24-hour RMT drivers' strike ran until midday Friday, and London Underground said more services ran than it had expected during the walkout. Seven more 24-hour strikes are planned for 17 and 19 December, 4 and 6 January, and 17, 23 and 25 February.
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute is unresolved, so Londoners face more disruption through the winter, including the run-up to Christmas.

stories.headline: Cabinet clears a revised delimitation bill ahead of Monday's special sitting
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved revised amendments on Friday that would raise the number of Lok Sabha seats in every state by a uniform 50%, while freezing each state's share of seats until 2051. That takes the House from 543 to about 814 seats (some reports say 850), and the plan is tied to 33% reservation for women. The bill has not yet been formally listed for the sitting that starts on 30 November.
stories.whyItMatters: Freezing state shares answers southern states' fear of losing influence. A constitutional amendment needs a two-thirds majority, and a similar bill failed in the Lok Sabha earlier this year.

stories.headline: Opposition to meet on Saturday as DMK sets its terms
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has called opposition floor leaders, including the DMK, AAP and BJD, to a meeting at 11:30 IST on Saturday. Congress says it backs the 33% women's quota but accuses the government of using it to push delimitation through. DMK chief M K Stalin said Tamil Nadu's 7.18% share of Lok Sabha seats must not fall, which the revised bill reportedly addresses.
stories.whyItMatters: Whether parties such as the DMK and BJD support the bill will decide if the government reaches two-thirds next week.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules, fee or visa changes today
stories.summary: GOV.UK lists no new Statement of Changes in November; HC 584 of 3 September is still the latest. Earned settlement, with 10-year ILR as the default and shorter routes for higher earners and some key workers, is still a proposal: the detailed rules have not been laid, with changes expected from December and implementation during 2027. The Immigration and Asylum Bill is now in the Lords.
stories.whyItMatters: Nothing changes yet for Skilled Worker holders planning ILR, but the earned settlement rules could be laid within weeks, so keep an eye on GOV.UK.

stories.headline: Home Office figures: Skilled Worker visas down 27%, settlement grants at a 16-year high
stories.summary: Official statistics for the year to September 2026, published on Thursday, show 57,000 Skilled Worker visas (down 27%), 31,000 Health and Care visas (down 44%) and 336,000 sponsored study visas (down 23%). Settlement grants rose 53% to 241,000, the most since 2010, and citizenship grants rose 10% to 265,000, including 27,700 to Indian nationals.
stories.whyItMatters: The figures show the effect of the 2025 tightening on work routes, and a wave of people reaching ILR and citizenship before the stricter settlement rules arrive.

stories.headline: NZ v India, 2nd Test: day 2 starts at 22:00 GMT tonight
stories.summary: New Zealand resume on 246 for 5 at Hagley Oval, with Tom Blundell on 53 not out in his 50th Test and Glenn Phillips on 36. Akash Deep has taken 2 for 52 so far, and India have not yet batted. The series is level at 0-0 after the draw in Wellington.
stories.whyItMatters: India need a win here to take the series. Early wickets on day 2 would stop New Zealand building a big total.

stories.headline: Premier League: Forest host Chelsea tonight; Arsenal v Man City on Sunday
stories.summary: Nottingham Forest play Chelsea at 20:00 GMT tonight. On Sunday, Everton host Liverpool at 12:00 and leaders Arsenal, with nine wins from 11 league games, host Manchester City at 16:30. A City win would cut the gap at the top to three points.
stories.whyItMatters: Sunday's match at the Emirates is the biggest of the weekend for the title race.

stories.headline: F1 Qatar GP: champion Antonelli tops both practice sessions
stories.summary: Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli was fastest in both Friday sessions at Lusail, ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell, with McLaren's Lando Norris third in FP2. Lewis Hamilton stopped on track with a suspected power-unit problem. Qualifying is at 18:00 GMT on Saturday.
stories.whyItMatters: The drivers' title is settled, but McLaren and Red Bull are still fighting for the constructors' championship.

stories.headline: Cygnus NG-25 cargo launch to the ISS on track for Sunday
stories.summary: NASA says the Cygnus XL freighter is set to launch on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral at 15:47 GMT on Sunday 29 November, with about 11,000 lb of cargo. The weather forecast is 60% favourable, and the backup slot is 15:24 GMT on Monday.
stories.whyItMatters: The stretched Cygnus XL carries more cargo per flight, restocking the station's science and supplies.

stories.headline: ISRO says Gaganyaan is not delayed, but there is still no launch date
stories.summary: ISRO chairman V Narayanan said this week that the first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight, carrying the Vyommitra robot, is in its final preparation phase and all rocket parts are ready. Earlier media reports suggested a slip from December to February 2027; ISRO has not confirmed a date.
stories.whyItMatters: The G1 flight is the key test before India's first crewed spaceflight.

stories.headline: Artemis III crew meet their Orion spacecraft
stories.summary: The Artemis III astronauts visited their Orion capsule at Kennedy Space Center. The mission will stay in low Earth orbit to rehearse docking with the Starship and Blue Moon landers, which clears the way for a landing on Artemis IV.
stories.whyItMatters: It is NASA's next step towards returning people to the Moon.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 closes up 0.8% at 10,698.81, its best week in about eight months
stories.summary: Friday 27 November close: FTSE 100 10,698.81, up 89.51 points (+0.84%); FTSE 250 up 0.9% at 24,314.72. Fresnillo, Antofagasta, Glencore and Anglo American gained 4-5% as copper had its best day since February after China's cabinet urged state-backed investors to steady its stock market, and Standard Chartered, Barclays and HSBC rose on the Bank of England's capital cut.
stories.whyItMatters: A broad rebound across global stocks and strength in miners and banks offset small falls in Unilever, Diageo and AstraZeneca.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty end lower as IT stocks are sold
stories.summary: Friday 27 November close: Sensex 83,339.26, down 989.33 points (-1.17%); Nifty 50 25,607.20, down 277.30 (-1.07%). The Nifty IT index fell 1.88%, with TCS, Infosys and HCL Tech among the biggest losers, while metals rose 1.40% and Bharat Electronics, JSW Steel and Titan gained. Small and mid caps ended slightly higher.
stories.whyItMatters: Profit-taking after a two-day rally, worries about US tariffs and expensive crude oil all weighed on the main indices.

stories.headline: Wall Street closes sharply higher in the Black Friday half-day
stories.summary: US markets shut early at 13:00 ET (18:00 GMT), so these are closes, compared with Wednesday: Dow 50,774.94 (+591.99, +1.18%), S&P 500 7,297.49 (+114.71, +1.60%) and Nasdaq Composite 24,129.50 (+543.70, +2.31%). Over the week the Dow rose 5.46%, the S&P 500 5.60% and the Nasdaq 6.68%, and the chip index jumped 4.69% on the day.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors bought back tech and chip stocks after this month's sell-off, on light holiday volume. Gold rose about 2% and the 10-year Treasury yield was near 4.89%.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 27 November 2026
headlines: EU summit ends with no budget deal; 45 billion euro Ukraine loan pushed to December
MoD writes to about 100,000 Strategic Reservists, the first such effort since the Cold War
Two Italian contractors killed by a drone in Kuwait; Iran denies involvement as Brent nears 97 dollars
Indian shares slip on IT selling while Asian markets rally; Wall Street reopens for a short session
New Zealand 246/5 at stumps on day one of the Christchurch Test against India

stories.headline: EU summit fails to agree the 2028-34 budget or the Ukraine loan
stories.summary: The special summit in Brussels ran about 14 hours on Thursday and was cut short, with day two cancelled. Seven frugal states refused the small-group format, and Slovakia, Hungary and the Czech Republic did not back the 45 billion euro loan to Ukraine. Leaders meet again around 17 December.
stories.whyItMatters: Ukraine's 2027 financing is still unsettled, and Macron says 31 December is the absolute deadline for the budget.

stories.headline: Two Italian defence technicians killed in a drone attack in Kuwait
stories.summary: The two Rheinmetall employees were servicing air-defence equipment, and a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were hurt. Kuwait and Italy say the drone came from Iran, while Tehran calls it a false flag and offered a joint investigation. Separately, the Saudi-led coalition says it hit 50 Houthi targets, and Saudi Arabia says one worker died in an attack on a refinery in Jazan.
stories.whyItMatters: European casualties bring NATO members closer to the Gulf conflict, and oil prices rose again overnight.

stories.headline: Zelensky warns of a new Russian mass strike; Poland incursions draw a Trump-Rutte warning
stories.summary: After Russian missiles and drones crossed into Polish airspace during attacks on Ukraine this week, Trump and NATO's Mark Rutte jointly urged Moscow not to widen the war. Zelensky says Kyiv has information that Russia plans another large strike in the coming days.
stories.whyItMatters: Poland has floated NATO shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine, which would mark a major escalation in the alliance's role.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases
stories.summary: Government data released on Thursday show 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths since May, across 8 of the DRC's 26 provinces. The outbreak is the Bundibugyo strain, which has no approved vaccine or treatment, and fighting is slowing the response, according to the WHO.
stories.whyItMatters: It is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with no medical tool to stop it.

stories.headline: Pablo Hernandez de Cos picked to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
stories.summary: Eurozone leaders chose the BIS general manager and former Bank of Spain governor to lead the ECB when Christine Lagarde steps down on 7 February. Formal confirmation is still needed.
stories.whyItMatters: With eurozone inflation at 4%, the new president inherits a possible rate rise as soon as December.

stories.headline: Thanksgiving storm cuts power to 800,000 on the US East Coast
stories.summary: New York declared a state of emergency for New York City, Long Island and other southern areas as gusts reached about 70 mph. Hundreds of flights were cancelled and more than 1,900 delayed.
stories.whyItMatters: Expect knock-on delays for transatlantic flights on one of the busiest US travel weekends.

stories.headline: MoD contacts about 100,000 Strategic Reservists, the first such effort since the Cold War
stories.summary: Letters signed by the heads of the Army, Navy and RAF ask former personnel who are still liable for recall to update their contact details and civilian skills, and invite volunteers for training. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called it a sensible, necessary precaution, and the veterans minister says mobilisation is not imminent.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a concrete step to rebuild reserve capacity after Russian incursions into Poland. Recall is still legally limited to a national emergency or an attack on the UK.

stories.headline: Bank of England lowers capital requirements for big banks and flags AI and cyber risks
stories.summary: The Financial Policy Committee finished its review of the bank capital framework. Major banks' Tier 1 requirements fall by about 0.5 percentage points of risk-weighted assets, against a system benchmark of around 13%, and the countercyclical buffer stays at 2%.
stories.whyItMatters: Freeing up capital could support lending. The Bank also warns that the Middle East conflict, public debt and stretched AI valuations could hit at the same time.

stories.headline: Delimitation-linked women's quota bill expected at Monday's special session
stories.summary: The government is expected to bring back a women's reservation bill tied to delimitation when Parliament sits from 30 November, though the agenda has not been published. A similar amendment fell short of a two-thirds majority in April, and NCP-SP has whipped its MPs to attend until 4 December.
stories.whyItMatters: Redrawing constituencies changes each state's share of Lok Sabha seats, and southern parties want a uniform rise before they give support.

stories.headline: Goyal says the India-US trade deal is nearing completion
stories.summary: Commerce minister Piyush Goyal says negotiations are close to done. Washington this week proposed higher Section 301 tariffs on India and 13 other economies if talks fail.
stories.whyItMatters: A deal would head off the new tariffs on Indian exports. No terms or date have been announced.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules, fee or visa changes overnight
stories.summary: The Home Office GOV.UK page shows nothing on visas, Skilled Worker, settlement, citizenship or fees since 18 November, and HC 584 of 3 September is still the latest Statement of Changes. Earned settlement, with 10-year ILR as the default, is government policy, but its rules have not been laid and it has no start date.

stories.headline: Student maintenance funds rise on Monday 30 November
stories.summary: Under HC 584, student visa applicants must show 1,570 pounds a month in London (up from 1,529) and 1,203 pounds elsewhere (up from 1,171) for applications made on or after 30 November 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: Anyone applying before Monday, including from India, is assessed at the old amounts.

stories.headline: NZ v India, 2nd Test, day 1: New Zealand 246/5
stories.summary: Shubman Gill won the toss and bowled, with Gurnoor Brar on debut. Tom Latham made 59 and Akash Deep took 2 for 52, before Tom Blundell (53 not out) and Glenn Phillips (36 not out) added an unbeaten 62 from 184 for 5.
stories.whyItMatters: The series is 0-0 after the Wellington draw, so India need early wickets on day 2 to stay on course for a win.

stories.headline: Ten-man Bournemouth win 2-1 at Celta Vigo and top the Europa League
stories.summary: Iago Aspas put Celta ahead, then Bafode Diakite was sent off after about 22 minutes. Bournemouth equalised early in the second half, and substitute Rayan scored the winner late on.
stories.whyItMatters: That is ten straight wins, and a home win over Viktoria Plzen in December should seal a top-eight finish.

stories.headline: Palace come from behind, Celtic win late, Sunderland held
stories.summary: Crystal Palace beat Real Sociedad 2-1 with a Mateta penalty and a late Dwight McNeil winner, Thomas Frank's first win in charge. Celtic won 2-1 at Torreense and Sunderland drew 1-1 with Jagiellonia, while AC Milan came from 2-0 down to beat Olympiacos 4-2.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab's 101st Electron puts a Japanese radar satellite into orbit
stories.summary: The Night Owls Never Sleep mission launched from New Zealand at 00:15 GMT and placed Synspective's StriX radar satellite into a 569 km orbit. It was Rocket Lab's 22nd launch this year. NG-25 Cygnus is still due to launch to the ISS on Sunday.
stories.whyItMatters: Small radar satellites can image through cloud and at night, and more of them means more frequent images for disaster and defence users.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty fall as IT stocks lose ground after a two-day rally
stories.summary: Live at 11:00 IST on Friday: Sensex 83,798.63 (down 529.96, -0.63%) and Nifty 50 25,733.40 (down 151.10, -0.58%), still trading. TCS, HCL Tech and Infosys led the losses, while metals, defence and small and mid caps rose, and oil rising on West Asia tensions weighed.

stories.headline: Asian markets rebound strongly on chip stocks; oil keeps climbing
stories.summary: At about 05:30 GMT on Friday the Kospi was up 4.2% at 4,906.93, the Nikkei 225 about 2.0% at 58,628.59, the Hang Seng about 2.1% and Shanghai 3.2%, all still trading. Brent rose 0.8% to 97.31 dollars and US crude about 3% to 86.18 dollars after a Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 jumped 1.75% on Thursday; Wall Street reopens for a half-day
stories.summary: Thursday 26 November close: FTSE 100 10,609.30, up 182.36 points (1.75%), led by miners, banks, Imperial Brands and Babcock. US markets were shut for Thanksgiving and reopen today for a shortened session; Wednesday 25 November close: Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (-0.25%), Nasdaq Composite 23,585.80 (-0.62%).

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 26 November 2026
headlines: Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery; a projectile hits Jazan port
EU leaders split over a 1.58 trillion euro budget and a 45 billion euro Ukraine loan
India recalls Parliament from Monday 30 November, with a delimitation bill expected
FTSE 100 closes up 1.8% at 10,609.30
India A knocked out by Sri Lanka A; the NZ v India decider starts at 22:00 GMT

stories.headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia widen to ports and the Ras Tanura refinery
stories.summary: The Houthis say they hit Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, on Wednesday. The coalition says it downed four drones there and saw only falling debris. A projectile caused minor damage at Jazan port, a drone was stopped near Jeddah port, missiles at Riyadh were intercepted, and rebel-run media report new Saudi strikes on Sanaa.
stories.whyItMatters: Attacks on Gulf energy sites and Red Sea ports put oil and shipping at risk; Brent rose 3.5% on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Iran says tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian state media say two tankers struck mines and caught fire in a restricted zone of the strait on Wednesday. Nobody has confirmed this independently. Brent was down 0.87% at 93.79 dollars a barrel at 09:39 GMT after Wednesday's jump.
stories.whyItMatters: About a fifth of the world's oil normally passes through Hormuz, so any confirmed attack there would move energy prices.

stories.headline: EU summit deadlocked on the 2028-34 budget and a Ukraine loan
stories.summary: Leaders in Brussels are split over a 1.58 trillion euro seven-year budget and a 45 billion euro loan to Ukraine that would be repaid only if Russia pays reparations. Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria object to the loan. Costa says talks could run into Friday, and a deal is now targeted for December.
stories.whyItMatters: Ukraine's funding for 2027 depends on the deal, and all 27 members must agree.

stories.headline: Explosion at Bangkok's Bangchak oil depot injures seven
stories.summary: A blast and fire hit the Bangchak facility in eastern Bangkok at about 14:45 local time, injuring seven people, four of them critically. The company says the fire was out within about half an hour, shut production units and is investigating the cause.
stories.whyItMatters: The site is one of Bangkok's main fuel plants, so investigators and the market will watch how long it stays offline.

stories.headline: Tube strike under way, the first of eight driver walkouts this winter
stories.summary: RMT drivers walked out at midday. The Circle and Piccadilly lines, including the Heathrow branch, did not run today, and service should be back to normal by about 18:00 on Friday. Seven more 24-hour strikes are set for 17 and 19 December, 4 and 6 January, and 17, 23 and 25 February.
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute over a voluntary four-day week for drivers is unresolved, so London faces repeated disruption into February.

stories.headline: Babcock wins an 8.7 billion pound MoD submarine support contract
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence awarded Babcock a five-year deal worth about 8.7 billion pounds to maintain and support Royal Navy submarines. Its shares rose 6.6%.
stories.whyItMatters: It secures work at the UK's submarine bases as defence spending rises.

stories.headline: Government recalls Parliament for 30 November to 3 December
stories.summary: Kiren Rijiju said the Lok Sabha will sit from Monday 30 November and the Rajya Sabha from 2 December, for essential government business, without naming bills. Congress says the aim is a delimitation bill that would raise Lok Sabha seats to 850, which failed in April, and calls it an attack on the Constitution. Opposition strategists meet on Friday at 16:30 IST.
stories.whyItMatters: Delimitation would redraw how seats are shared between states and is tied to women's reservation, and passing it needs a two-thirds majority.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or fee changes today
stories.summary: The Home Office's GOV.UK page shows no visa, settlement, fee or citizenship announcements on 24 to 26 November, and no new Statement of Changes. The latest items are from 18 to 19 November: the Immigration and Asylum Bill passed the Commons and went to the Lords, and Professor Jackline Wahba became chair of the Migration Advisory Committee.
stories.whyItMatters: Earned settlement is confirmed but has no in-force date yet. The rules are due to start being laid from the December Immigration Rules and phased in during 2027, so Indian Skilled Workers should watch the December Statement of Changes.

stories.headline: Sri Lanka A knock India A out of the Rising Stars Asia Cup
stories.summary: India A made 317 for 8 in Doha, with 78 from Abhishek Sharma. Sri Lanka A won by eight wickets with 51 balls left, led by centuries from Lasith Croospulle (116) and Sineth Jayawardena (105). Sri Lanka A play the final on Sunday 29 November.
stories.whyItMatters: It is an early exit for a strong India A squad that included several senior internationals.

stories.headline: NZ v India second Test starts tonight at 22:00 GMT
stories.summary: The toss at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, is at 21:30 GMT. The series is 0-0 after the draw in Wellington, so India must win to level it. NZ seamer Blair Tickner is out injured and Matt Fisher has been called up.
stories.whyItMatters: India are fourth in the World Test Championship and need wins to stay in the race for the final.

stories.headline: FCC approves SpaceX's plan for a million data-centre satellites
stories.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission authorised SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to one million satellites for computing in orbit. The first satellites must launch by November 2033 and the full system must be running by 2040. There was no major ISRO or NASA mission news today.
stories.whyItMatters: A system that size would dwarf every satellite now in orbit and adds to concerns about space debris and astronomy.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 closes up 1.8% at 10,609.30 on bid talk, miners and defence
stories.summary: Thursday close: FTSE 100 10,609.30, up 182.36 points (1.75%). Imperial Brands rose about 13% after Altria said it is considering a possible cash offer, miners rallied on higher metal prices, and Babcock added 6.6%. The FTSE 250 rose 1.9%.
stories.whyItMatters: London recovered Wednesday's tariff and inflation losses, with thin volumes because US markets were shut.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty end a choppy day higher, led by IT and realty
stories.summary: Thursday close: Sensex 84,328.59, up 390.31 points (0.46%), and Nifty 50 25,884.50, up 65.25 (0.25%), a third straight gain. Indices gave up early gains on oil worries before IT stocks such as TCS and HCL Tech and property shares led a recovery.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign buying is holding up Indian stocks despite the US tariff threat and higher oil prices.

stories.headline: Wall Street closed for Thanksgiving; Wednesday's late rebound still stands
stories.summary: US exchanges are closed today. Wednesday 25 November close: Dow 50,182.95 (up 0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (down 0.25%), Nasdaq Composite 23,585.80 (down 0.62%), after a sharp early drop on inflation data and the US tariff plan.
stories.whyItMatters: Friday's short session and any oil moves from the Gulf will set the tone for next week.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 26 November 2026
headlines: Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh are intercepted; blast hits Sanaa as Brent jumps 3.5%
Wall Street recovers from a deep intraday slump; US markets shut today for Thanksgiving
India rejects the US excess capacity finding behind a 25% tariff threat
London Tube strike from midday today, with no Tube service after 9pm
Liverpool win 3-0 in Bruges; Manchester United draw 2-2 at Sporting

stories.headline: Houthi missiles at Riyadh intercepted as strikes hit Sanaa
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh overnight, while an explosion shook Sanaa after air strikes near its airport. UKMTO logged a tanker reporting a blast from an unknown projectile about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai, with no injuries or damage. Houthi claims of hits on Ras Tanura and the Jeddah and Jizan ports remain unconfirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: The Yemen front is now reaching Saudi cities and Gulf shipping lanes. Brent settled 3.5% higher at 94.61 dollars on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Fuel tanker fire on a Cairo ring road kills at least 31
stories.summary: A fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on a major highway around Cairo on Wednesday evening, setting vehicles alight. Egypt's health ministry put the toll at at least 31 dead and 21 injured.
stories.whyItMatters: The toll may rise: officials say several survivors have burns over most of their bodies.

stories.headline: RMT Tube strike runs from midday today to midday Friday
stories.summary: London Underground workers in the RMT walk out from 12:00 today until 11:59 on Friday over new working arrangements after talks failed. TfL says the Piccadilly and Circle lines will not run today, all lines are disrupted from noon and the network shuts after 21:00, with normal service by about 18:00 Friday. The Overground runs as usual.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the first of eight strike dates announced, with more set for December, January and February.

stories.headline: BBC journalists vote for strike action over 500 million pound cuts
stories.summary: NUJ members at the BBC backed strikes by 79.4% on a 75% turnout, and 91.3% backed action short of a strike, over cuts, forced redundancies and workloads. The mandate lasts 12 months and no dates have been set.
stories.whyItMatters: Walkouts could disrupt BBC news programmes while the corporation pushes through deep savings.

stories.headline: India rejects US claim of structural excess capacity
stories.summary: After the US Trade Representative named India among 16 economies it says add to global overcapacity and proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, or 17% with a trade deal, the Commerce Ministry said India has no structural excess capacity in any sector. It said trade concerns should be handled in the bilateral trade agreement talks.
stories.whyItMatters: The tariffs are only proposed, but they put a clock on the India-US trade deal.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets aside order for CBI and ED checks on Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant quashed an Allahabad High Court order that had told the CBI and ED to verify disproportionate-assets allegations against Rahul Gandhi. The case returns to a fresh High Court bench, which must hear him and first decide whether the petition is maintainable.
stories.whyItMatters: It removes an immediate investigative threat to Gandhi, though the allegations themselves were not ruled on.

stories.headline: Constitution Day turns political; 26/11 victims remembered
stories.summary: India marks the 77th Constitution Day today, also the anniversary of the 2008 Mumbai attacks. PM Modi used an op-ed to attack Congress over the Emergency, while Congress holds Samvidhan Raksha marches in several states over alleged voter-roll deletions.
stories.whyItMatters: Voter-roll accuracy is becoming the opposition's main theme for the 2027 state polls.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office immigration announcements
stories.summary: GOV.UK's Home Office news through 25 November shows nothing on visas, settlement, fees or citizenship, and no new Statement of Changes has been reported this week. Earned settlement remains confirmed policy with no start date because its rules have not been laid. It makes 10 years the default route to ILR, 5 years for those earning over 50,271 pounds, with B2 English required.
stories.whyItMatters: Skilled Worker visa holders, including many Indian nationals, should keep applying under the current rules until the new rules are laid and dated.

stories.headline: Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League
stories.summary: Alexander Isak scored early and late and Florian Wirtz curled in a third at the Jan Breydel Stadium. Liverpool have 12 points from five league-phase games and host Porto next.
stories.whyItMatters: It keeps Liverpool in the top eight, the places that skip the knockout play-off round.

stories.headline: Manchester United draw 2-2 at Sporting; Bayern lose to Lille
stories.summary: United were held in Lisbon and had a late Sporting own goal ruled out for a foul. PSG drew with Roma, Lille beat Bayern Munich and Inter won at Stuttgart.
stories.whyItMatters: United's draw leaves their place in the top eight in doubt with three league-phase games left.

stories.headline: Cricket today: India A semi-final at 10:00, Christchurch Test at 22:00 GMT
stories.summary: India A play unbeaten Sri Lanka A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-final in Doha from 10:00 GMT, with the final on Sunday. At 22:00 GMT New Zealand and India start the second and final Test at Hagley Oval with the series level.
stories.whyItMatters: India need to win in Christchurch to take the series.

stories.headline: Europa League tonight: Bournemouth, Palace, Sunderland and Celtic
stories.summary: Bournemouth visit Celta Vigo at 17:45 UK time. At 20:00 Crystal Palace host Real Sociedad, Sunderland host Jagiellonia and Celtic visit Torreense.
stories.whyItMatters: Matchday 5 of 8 is where top-eight places in the league phase start to settle.

stories.headline: Quiet night for space; Cygnus NG-25 still due on Sunday
stories.summary: No major ISRO, NASA or other mission news broke overnight. Northrop Grumman's NG-25 cargo flight to the ISS remains listed for a Falcon 9 launch from Cape Canaveral on Sunday 29 November.

stories.headline: Wall Street claws back an AI and inflation sell-off; FTSE slipped 0.38%
stories.summary: Wednesday close: Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (-0.25%), Nasdaq Composite 23,585.80 (-0.62%), after the S&P had been down as much as 3.2% on hot PCE inflation, the US tariff plan and AI-stock selling. The FTSE 100 closed at 10,426.94, down 0.38%. US markets are closed today for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday.
stories.whyItMatters: Markets now treat a December Fed rate rise as likely, keeping pressure on borrowing costs worldwide.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty extend Wednesday's rally on IT buying, still trading
stories.summary: Live at 09:20 IST: Sensex 84,326.40 (+388.12, +0.46%) and Nifty 50 25,880.00 (+60.75, +0.23%), led by IT stocks. Foreign investors have bought for 11 sessions in a row, about 14 billion dollars this month.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign buying is shielding Indian stocks from the US tariff threat, though Brent above 95 dollars and a weak rupee are risks.

stories.headline: Asian stocks rebound; Bank of Korea reported to raise rates
stories.summary: In Thursday's session the Nikkei 225 was up about 1.2%, the Kospi about 1.7% and the Hang Seng about 1.5%. One report says the Bank of Korea raised its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25%; this is not yet confirmed by the central bank.
stories.whyItMatters: A rate rise in Korea would show inflation pressure spreading beyond the US.
